approvalScope: Only visible course organization, readability, figure-label composition and caption identification in the six exact assigned desktop/mobile screenshots, opened once each in one batch
summary: The complete desktop and mobile pages preserve the approved English sequence, definitions, two concept separators, one nonblank diagram and its identifiable English caption. Text wraps within the columns without apparent overlap or clipping. The initial viewports are readable, and fig-57's English region labels and named points remain distinguishable at the reported 640px and 358px media widths. The Chinese critical-temperature math subscript is intentionally retained beside an English gloss; this PASS is not full-English formula/accessibility, all-glyph, headed, production or source/figure approval.

images.observation: Centered English title and body column, readable definition groups, fig-57 with separate Figure 57 caption, two unobstructed concept separators and the final density conclusion are visible. No gross collision, blank media or clipped ending is apparent. The inequality retains its Chinese critical subscript as expected.

Actual N40 initial viewport, not polarization: the title, breadcrumb, isotherm/fixed-mass and equilibrium/vapor/condensation definitions and AK/CK explanation are readable and separated inside the column.

All four English region labels, C/K, A/B, p/V and origin are visible with clearances. Solid/dashed curves and four texture types are distinguishable and contained. No label overlap or clipped edge is apparent. Caption is outside this figure-only capture.

The complete mobile course wraps into one column with all three concept groups, fig-57 and its centered English caption, the saturation/mass passage, inequality gloss, conditional ideal-gas explanation and final conclusion. Separators and paragraphs do not collide or extend horizontally outside the page. No blank media or clipped ending is apparent.

The N40 title and breadcrumb wrap cleanly without overlapping each other or the body. Initial definitions are readable within the margins. The critical-temperature passage reaches the lower viewport boundary normally; this is not a cropped or missing course object.

The four region labels remain readable and unoccluded at reported 358px media width. Named points, dashed boundaries, solid curve, K junction and textures are visibly intact. The right-edge V is complete, and no other axis/label is apparently clipped. Caption inspection uses the whole-page view.

courseFlow.conclusion: Initial definitions and left-boundary/liquid discussion precede the figure; coexistence and phase-mass explanation follow its caption and first separator; below/above-critical behavior follows the second separator and ends with continuous density changes. The complete visible sequence is intact on both viewports.

readabilityAndLayout.conclusion: The initial viewports provide readable English text, clear line/paragraph spacing and contained wrapping. Complete-page views show no apparent text collision, horizontal truncation, blank media or clipped final paragraph. This assesses visible layout, not a new child-comprehension test.

captions.conclusion: Figure 57 is an identifiable English caption centered below the figure and separated from the following separator/prose on both complete-page views. Figure-only screenshots exclude captions and cannot supply additional caption evidence.

figureLabelsAndContext.conclusion: Liquid, Liquid + saturated vapor, Gas and Unsaturated vapor are visible in separate clearances with distinguishable horizontal/vertical/dotted/diagonal textures. C/K, A/B and p/V/origin are present. The visible diagram supports the already-reviewed English AK/BK, CK and critical-endpoint referents; no new source relationship or geometry approval is inferred.

retainedCriticalMath.conclusion: The Chinese critical-temperature subscript is visibly retained next to the English temperature/inequality gloss on both complete-page views. It is intentionally not localized, and is not a new defect or an all-English formula/accessibility approval.
